One ward. Four facts. Two buttons.

How deep, where to go, which roads are closing, and whether a bridge is in the way. Everything else on the officer screen is deliberately absent.

What is NOT here, on purpose

No district total. No other wards. No shelter occupancy. No probability, no cost-loss table, no override. Every extra number competes with the four that matter to a person deciding whether to leave.

The two buttons are the point

Radar cannot see water standing between buildings in a dense city, which is exactly why the 2019 Patna disaster is missing from our own flood map. A person outside their door is the only sensor that sees it, and I cannot leave is the only source for that fact anywhere in the system.

Both write straight into the officer's Citizen reports and Help queue in the left nav. Same backend, opposite ends.

Built for a bad phone

One page, no framework, ward remembered locally. It has to work on 2G during a flood, which is the only time it matters.
